front.title: AAC Evidence Bundle

abstract.t: This document defines the AAC Evidence Bundle, a portable presentation and verification container for an Agent Action Capsule and the records that make its evidentiary claim intelligible. A permalink carries a bundle in its URL fragment, an offline HTML report carries a bundle in its shell, and a hosted report serves a bundle at its URL. The bundle does not alter any enclosed Capsule. It declares its citation closure and any missing cited records, carries verified disclosure preimages as a bundle-level overlay, separates three different completeness claims, can carry the producer's signed declaration of what it offers in each category of evidence, and permits independently specified extension blocks and countersignatures: signatures by a party other than the producer over the bundle digest, each accompanied by a statement of which claims that party recomputed and with what result.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: A Capsule proves the identity and claimed content of one action. An audit report normally needs more: the report Capsule, its chain of judgments or adjudications, the turns cited by those records, selected disclosed preimages, and the log evidence that supports a claim about coverage. Passing these items as unrelated files produces a presentation that a verifier cannot describe precisely.

The AAC Evidence Bundle is that unit of evidence. It is deliberately a presentation-layer object: the Capsules in records retain their original bytes, identities, signatures, and registrations. The same bundle can be encoded in a URL fragment, embedded in an offline HTML shell, or obtained from a hosted report URL. These are transports for one object, not distinct evidence formats.

section.name: Conventions and Definitions
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

dd.t: An AAC Evidence Bundle as defined in .
The Capsule identified by the Bundle's root member. The Bundle's evidence claim is made from this Capsule outward through its declared closure.
The lowercase-hex SHA-256 digest of UTF8(JCS(value)), using over the whole recursively canonicalized JSON value with no member filtering, as defined by .
A countersignature is a signature by a party other than the producer over a bundle digest, accompanied by a statement of which claims that party recomputed and with what result. A report is a bundle.

The party that makes a countersignature. A countersigner works in the manner of an Auditor : it independently recomputes checks over a Bundle it was given and signs a statement of the results -- a list of what it recomputed, never an opinion. A countersigner MAY register that statement as a Signed Statement with a Transparency Service, in which case the entry carries the Receipt; the Receipt proves that the statement is in that log and says nothing about the Bundle. Which producers a countersigner accepts Bundles from is its own admission rule, outside this document.
An entry in countersignatures whose signer key is the producer's key (). It is well-formed and is rendered as not independent.

section.t: countersignatures is a member name. An entry is a statement by a party other than the producer that it recomputed named checks over the bundle digest, in the manner of an Auditor . It is not a COSE countersignature , not a Receipt , and not a Transparency Service function.

dd.t: The disclosure state of an eligible member absent from the Bundle-level disclosure overlay. It is neither an empty value nor a verification failure.

section.t: The terms "Capsule", "capsule_id", chain.parent_capsule_id, references, seq, leaf_index, and log_coordinates are as defined in .

section.name: Evidence Bundle Object
section.t: A Bundle is a JSON object with this shape. Ellipses denote values defined by this document or a registered extension; they do not authorize untyped replacement formats.

bundle_version and bundle_kind are REQUIRED and MUST be respectively "2" and "evidence-bundle/v2". root, records, and completeness are REQUIRED, except that an empty-history Bundle () has no root. root is the lowercase-hex capsule_id of one record in records. Every records element MUST be an unmodified Capsule object conforming to ; duplicate capsule_id values are not permitted. All other members shown are OPTIONAL unless a claim in this document requires them. A receiver MUST reject an object with an unknown bundle_version or bundle_kind as an AAC Evidence Bundle, rather than silently applying version-2 verification rules.

payloads_mode states whether the producer included all payload material it chose to carry (all), only a selected subset (selected), or none (none). A Bundle whose payloads_mode is none carries no disclosures member. selection, when present, names the certificate mode of completeness_certificate (). suppressed_fields names fields intentionally not carried by the Bundle; it does not turn an absent disclosure into an empty value or a failure.

section.name: Empty-History Bundles
section.t: An empty-history Bundle shows that a log stream has no history to disclose. A stream that was never started and a history that was cleared read the same. Clearing a history starts a new stream, with a new log_id, under the same key. It never rewrites or truncates the old stream's log, and a checkpoint that does so is inconsistent with that log's earlier checkpoints.
An empty-history Bundle has an empty records array and no root member. root MUST be absent exactly when records is empty. In an empty-history Bundle:

li.t: completeness.records_mode MUST be complete, completeness.missing MUST be absent or empty, and completeness.payloads_mode MUST be none;
completeness_certificate, disclosures and disclosure_record MUST be absent;
checkpoint, with checkpoint.cose, SHOULD be present when the stream has a checkpoint: its first checkpoint, or its latest one while it still holds no record. A stream that was never started has none.

section.t: A Bundle with no root that is not a well-formed empty-history Bundle is malformed.

A verifier reports a well-formed empty-history Bundle as no history. It is well formed: a verifier MUST NOT report it as failed, and MUST NOT report it as an absence (). Of its claims (), graph closure passes, since there is nothing to close, and interval coverage and per-record membership are not established, with the finding no_records. When checkpoint.cose verifies, the verifier reports the checkpoint's signed timestamp with the result, as no history since that time. Otherwise it reports no history without a date.

section.name: Citation Closure
section.t: Citation closure is declared, not assumed. Starting at root, a producer MUST traverse chain.parent_capsule_id and every references[].digest transitively through completeness.closure_depth edges. The default depth is 2 when the member is absent: report to judgments or adjudications, then to turns. A producer using a different depth MUST state that non-negative JSON integer explicitly.

For each target reached within that depth, the Bundle MUST either supply the cited Capsule in records with a matching identity or list its digest once in completeness.missing. A target MUST NOT be silently dropped. records_mode MUST be complete exactly when missing is absent or empty, and MUST be declared_incomplete exactly when it is non-empty. A verifier MUST report the latter as declared incomplete, not as complete and not as an unexplained failure. A supplied record whose computed capsule_id does not match the chain target or reference digest is not supplied evidence for that target.

The closure declaration says nothing about records beyond its stated depth. A verifier MUST report the depth it applied and MUST NOT infer unbounded ancestry or citation completeness from the presence of a short chain.

section.name: Bundle-Level Disclosures
section.t: disclosures is a Bundle-level overlay keyed first by the enclosed Capsule's capsule_id, then by the disclosure member name:

It has the same eligibility and DE-3 digest rule as the per-Capsule Disclosure Envelope in . The member name selects that draft's registered committed-digest path in the specified Capsule. For every disclosed member, a verifier MUST compute JSON-DIGEST(revealed preimage) and compare it to the committed digest at that registered path in that records element. A match is REVEALED; a mismatch is a failed verification of that disclosed content. A member absent from this overlay is WITHHELD, never blank and never failed.

The overlay is carried once per Bundle rather than by wrapping each Capsule in {capsule, disclosures}. It MUST NOT alter an enclosed Capsule or its capsule_id. An overlay key not naming a supplied record, or a member not eligible under the Disclosure Envelope registry, is a disclosure finding and MUST NOT be treated as a successful revelation. disclosure_record, when present, identifies the Capsule that records the act of sealing or issuing these disclosures; it is evidence about that act and does not replace the DE-3 check.

section.name: Completeness Claims and Log Membership
section.t: completeness_certificate and checkpoint, when supplied, support three separate claims. A verifier MUST report each claim independently. The composed/v1 extension adds a fourth claim, composition closure (), which is reported separately from these three.

li.t: Graph closure: every citation reached under is supplied with matching identity or explicitly listed in completeness.missing.

Interval coverage: the claimed sequence interval is bound to a checkpointed range root. Without a verified Receipt over the checkpoint from a Transparency Service, or a verified checkpoint signature, this is only relative to a producer-asserted checkpoint.
Per-record membership: every supplied record is bound to its claimed log position under that range root, and, for a range, every other leaf in the interval is accounted for ().

section.t: Per-record membership is the claim a range certificate makes about the records in its interval: interval coverage binds the leaf values, and per-record membership says what each leaf is. A verifier MUST ignore members of completeness_certificate that this document does not define; they MUST NOT change any result it reports.

The certificate MUST state its log_id, range root, first and last seq, and the proof material that binds that range root to checkpoint. A signed range proof that binds only the first and last record proves endpoint inclusion only: an interior record can be deleted or replaced while such a proof still passes. A verifier MUST NOT report whole-range completeness from endpoint inclusion alone. A verifier MUST verify an included Receipt over the checkpoint, or the checkpoint signature, before reporting interval coverage or per-record membership as independently verified. Otherwise it MUST explicitly label those claims checkpoint_unverified and describe them as relative to a producer-asserted checkpoint. The portable checkpoint signature member is checkpoint.cose, an unpadded base64url CLL COSE checkpoint. A verifier that implements this member MUST verify it and require its log identifier, MMR size, and root to equal the certificate and checkpoint values before removing the qualifier.

For the third claim, every supplied record MUST either carry a membership entry within the declared interval or be explicitly listed in completeness.missing. A membership entry or record whose seq is outside the interval MUST be rejected. Each membership entry MUST carry log_coordinates stating its claimed position and an inclusion proof to the certificate's range root. The base profile's terms apply exactly: seq is the 1-based log position and leaf_index = seq - 1 is the zero-based MMR index. log_coordinates states which index is used. The verifier MUST verify every inclusion proof at its stated leaf_index, require the proof's leaf_index to equal that coordinate and its size to equal checkpoint.mmr_size, and bind the record to the range root; it MUST NOT substitute an endpoint proof for a missing per-record proof. A record without a valid proof may remain usable for graph closure but does not satisfy per-record membership.

section.name: Certificate Modes
section.t: completeness.selection names the mode in which completeness_certificate is read:

li.t: Absent (the Bundle has no selection member): a range certificate, as described above. Its interval ends at the checkpoint's last leaf.
producer-selected: a producer-selected certificate ().

section.t: This document defines no other value. A verifier that meets a selection value it does not implement, including a value that is not a string (null among them), MUST report interval coverage and per-record membership as not established (finding certificate_mode_unsupported). It MUST NOT report either claim as failed because of the mode, MUST NOT read the certificate under another mode, and MUST NOT report the Bundle as invalid on that ground. Graph closure, disclosures, extensions and countersignatures are unaffected.

The same rule applies to a verifier that predates a mode: a verifier that does not implement producer-selected certificates reports such a Bundle's interval coverage and per-record membership as not established, never as failed. A Bundle in a mode the verifier lacks is unverified in that respect; it is not evidence of tampering, and reporting it as invalid would make an honest Bundle indistinguishable from an altered one. The selection member is the producer's to write, and so is any edit to a Bundle after it is made: setting an unknown mode can turn a failing claim into one that is not established, but never into one that is established ().

section.name: Producer-Selected Certificates
section.t: A producer-selected Bundle carries records that its producer chose from a log, each proven on its own, and makes no claim about the records between them. Its completeness.selection is producer-selected. Its certificate carries log_id, range_root and memberships. It carries no range: first_seq, last_seq, body_digests and range_proof are not part of it, and a verifier does not read them. It MUST NOT carry non_record_leaves ().
A verifier that implements this mode:

li.t: reports interval coverage as not established (finding selection_not_checkable): there is no interval;

verifies per-record membership record by record. range_root MUST equal the checkpoint's root, and the certificate's log_id the checkpoint's log_id. Each record's membership entry MUST carry log_coordinates naming the checkpoint's log_id, a seq of at least 1 that no other entry claims, and leaf_index = seq - 1, and an inclusion proof at that index whose size equals checkpoint.mmr_size and that binds the record's capsule_id to the root. A membership entry for a record the Bundle does not carry is a failure. Otherwise the rules of apply, including the checkpoint_unverified label;
reports a certificate that carries non_record_leaves as invalid.

section.t: When checkpoint.cose does not verify, or a stated value (including the certificate's log_id) contradicts it, the checkpoint anchors no record: the verifier reports per-record membership as not established, labelled checkpoint_unverified, except that a certificate that carries non_record_leaves still fails it.

A producer-selected Bundle is therefore never complete as to its log: a verifier MUST NOT report it as such, and its best result is that every carried record is a member of the checkpointed log. A changed record or proof fails per-record membership exactly as in a range Bundle. Graph closure, which is about citations, not log positions, is unaffected by the mode.

section.name: Non-Record Leaves
section.t: A log can hold leaves that are not records. The Evidence Layer reserves the record_type value padding for records a store appends so that a checkpoint's size falls on a bucket boundary (its Section 12.1). A store that pads before every checkpoint usually has a padding leaf at the checkpoint's last leaf, so a range ending there always covers one. A range certificate covers such leaves in its member non_record_leaves, which carries each one in full:

non_record_leaves is an array. Each element is an object with seq, the leaf's 1-based log position within [first_seq, last_seq], and content, the leaf's content. A digest alone is not accepted in place of content: a bare leaf value could be the identifier of a Capsule that the Bundle thereby hides. Members of an element other than seq and content are ignored.

The padding leaf. This document defines one non-record leaf type, padding. The members of a padding record are those of Section 12.1: record_type padding, epistemic_type producer_claim, and store_nonce, 32 bytes as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. That document fixes the members but not their serialization or the record's identifier, so this document states both for a padding leaf in a Bundle. Its content is a JSON object with exactly four members: those three and capsule_id. capsule_id is 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters, and is the JSON-DIGEST () of the object formed by the other three members. The leaf value is capsule_id. A store's local-only producer envelope (signature, key_id) is not part of content. (Moving this rule into the Evidence Layer awaits a later revision of that document.)
Checking an element. A verifier reads the elements in order. For each one:

li.t: An element that is not an object is malformed (finding non_record_leaf_element_invalid).

A seq that is not an integer within [first_seq, last_seq], that any membership entry states in its log_coordinates (whether or not that entry is otherwise valid), or that is the seq of an earlier element, is invalid (finding non_record_leaf_seq_invalid); the element accounts for no position.
Otherwise the element accounts for its seq. Then:
when content is not an object, or its record_type is not a string, the element is malformed (finding non_record_leaf_malformed);

the verifier recomputes the leaf value from the other three members and requires it to equal both content.capsule_id and body_digests[seq - first_seq]; otherwise the leaf does not match (finding non_record_leaf_mismatch).

section.t: A non_record_leaves value that is not an array is malformed (finding non_record_leaves_malformed) and accounts for no position.

Per-position accounting. For per-record membership over a range, every seq in [first_seq, last_seq] MUST be accounted for by exactly one of a record's membership entry and a non_record_leaves element. Each position is then:

li.t: verified: a record's verified membership, or a padding leaf that recomputes to its body digest;
unsupported: a leaf of a type the verifier does not implement; or
unaccounted: neither, or an element that failed a check above (finding membership_record_missing for a position with neither).

section.t: Any failure fails per-record membership, whatever else is unsupported. When nothing fails and some position is unsupported, per-record membership is not established: the verifier MUST NOT report it as established, and MUST NOT report it as failed. Otherwise the rules of apply. A verifier that implements this member therefore no longer rejects a range because it contains padding records, as Section 12.1 requires. A verifier that does not implement the member ignores it, as it ignores any member it does not know, and then reports every padding position as missing, which fails per-record membership. A producer therefore SHOULD NOT emit non_record_leaves to readers that do not implement this revision; until it can, a producer-selected certificate states what it can prove without it.

A non-record leaf is not a record. It never appears in records, never counts as a record for graph closure, disclosures or any count a verifier reports, and is never the target of a citation. Leaves other than padding, such as a store's checkpoint stamps, are not covered by this document. A range over a log that contains one is reported, at best, as not established through non_record_leaf_type_unsupported; a producer that needs a Bundle over such a log without that result uses a producer-selected certificate.

section.name: Category Coverage
section.t: category_coverage, when present, is the producer's signed declaration of what it offers in each category of a named category set: for each category, exactly one status. It answers the categories field of an Evidence Request (), and a producer MAY include it without one. It declares; it does not prove. A verifier checks that it is well formed, who signed it, and whether it is consistent with what the Bundle carries. It never establishes that the producer offers everything it declares, or that nothing exists in a category declared absent.

set is REQUIRED, a non-empty string naming a category set (). A set whose identifier begins x- is private: it is not registered, and a verifier never treats it as known. categories is REQUIRED, a non-empty object keyed by category name; each value is an object with status and, where required, policy_uri. request_digest, OPTIONAL, is the digest of the Evidence Request this declaration answers, computed as computes a request digest, in lowercase hexadecimal. signer and signature are OPTIONAL, and present together or not at all. Members not defined here are ignored: they never make the member malformed, and a signature covers them.
The member is part of the bundle digest (), so a countersignature binds it.

section.name: Statuses
section.t: Each category has exactly one status, written in upper case:

tr.td: evidence in this category is offered
only some evidence in this category is offered
evidence in this category may exist and is not released to this requester
evidence in this category was destroyed or has expired
the producer states that it holds nothing in this category
the producer does not state which of the other statuses applies, under the policy policy_uri names

section.t: AVAILABLE, PARTIAL, WITHHELD and DELETED are retention states of the Evidence Layer , with the same meanings, applied to a category rather than to one record's payload. This document defines UNDISCLOSED and ABSENT. ABSENT is the producer's asserted absence in the Evidence Layer's sense ("Three Kinds of No"): its own unproven claim about its own store, never a non-membership proof and never the requester's recorded absence of . The retention state LEGAL_HOLD is not a status: it changes what may happen to evidence, not what is offered.

UNDISCLOSED MUST carry policy_uri, an absolute URI (, Section 4.3) naming the policy under which the status is not disclosed; policy_uri MAY accompany any other status. WITHHELD and UNDISCLOSED are different statements and MUST NOT be conflated: WITHHELD says evidence may exist and is not released; UNDISCLOSED says nothing about whether any exists.

section.name: Signature
section.t: signer.key_id is a 32-byte Ed25519 public key as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. signature is the Ed25519 signature, as 128 lowercase hexadecimal characters, under that key over the signing input
section.artwork: UTF8(JCS({"category_coverage": <the member without signature>, "root": <the Bundle's root>}))
section.t: Including root binds the declaration to the root record of the Bundle it was made for: a signed declaration copied into a Bundle with another root does not verify. It does not bind the rest of the Bundle; a Bundle with the same root and other records carries it unchanged, and only the bundle digest () tells the two Bundles apart. The signature attributes the declaration to the holder of the key. It does not establish who that holder is; a verifier MAY compare signer.key_id with the producer's keys () and report the result.

section.name: Verifier Properties
section.t: A verifier that implements this member reports the following properties, each as exactly one of PASS, FAIL, NOT_PRESENT, NOT_CHECKED and INCONCLUSIVE, as the definition of each property below assigns them. A Bundle without the member has no category properties.

dd.t: PASS when the member is as described above, including a policy_uri for every UNDISCLOSED status; otherwise FAIL. When it is FAIL, every other property is NOT_CHECKED.

NOT_PRESENT when the member carries no signature; PASS when the signature verifies; FAIL otherwise, including when the signing input has no JCS serialization (for example, a number JCS cannot represent).
NOT_PRESENT for a private (x-) set; INCONCLUSIVE when the verifier does not know the set; FAIL when it knows the set and a declared category is not one of its names; PASS otherwise.

NOT_CHECKED when the verifier cannot assign every record the Bundle carries to a category, or to none (the set's definition says how): a record it cannot assign could be in any category; FAIL when a record the Bundle carries belongs to a category declared ABSENT or WITHHELD; PASS otherwise. A record in a DELETED or UNDISCLOSED category is not a contradiction, and an AVAILABLE category with no record in the Bundle is not one either: the Bundle may cover less than the producer offers.

section.t: Each property stands alone. A verifier MUST report them separately and MUST NOT combine them, or the statuses, into a count, a percentage, a score or a claim of completeness. It MUST NOT report a PASS of every property as proof that the producer offered everything it holds. A FAIL of category_coverage_form, category_coverage_signature or category_coverage_consistency is a failed check of the Bundle; the other properties are reported and change no other result. Category coverage is reported apart from the completeness claims of and changes none of them.
A verifier that does not implement this member follows the rule for any member it does not know: it reports nothing about it, and the member stays covered by the bundle digest.

section.name: Typed Extensions
section.t: extensions, when present, is an object keyed by a registered Evidence Bundle extension kind. The member name declares the kind and its value is that kind's block. The extension kind registry is Specification Required. A registered specification defines its block shape and any semantic checks. For example, a company-side row model such as report/v1 is permitted only as such an extension; this neutral core does not define, parse, or own its rows.

Extensions are included in the bundle digest (). A verifier that does not implement a registered extension kind MUST preserve its integrity status as digest-covered, report the block as uninterpreted, and MUST NOT apply that block's semantics. An unknown kind MUST NOT alter the core Capsule, closure, disclosure, or membership checks.

section.name: The producer-key/v1 Extension
section.t: The producer-key/v1 extension kind declares the key of the producer that assembled the Bundle:

public_key is the producer's 32-byte Ed25519 public key as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. The block carries one key. A producer MUST NOT add other members to the block, and a verifier MUST ignore any it finds. Like every extension, the block is covered by the bundle digest, so a countersignature's over binds the declaration, and adding, removing, or changing the declaration afterwards makes that entry invalid.

A verifier that implements this kind uses public_key for one purpose only: it adds the key to the producer's keys when determining independence (), so that a countersign/v1 entry whose signer.key_id equals it is reported as not independent. The declaration can only cause an entry to be reported as not independent. It MUST NOT cause any entry to be reported as independent, resolved, or valid, and it MUST NOT change any other result. It is not a claim of identity or of authority, and a verifier MUST NOT present it as one. The absence of this extension says nothing about whether any entry is independent.

The block is malformed when it is not an object, or when public_key is absent, is not a string, or is not exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. A verifier MUST ignore a malformed block when determining independence, MUST NOT fail the Bundle or any claim because of it, and still treats the block as digest-covered.

section.name: The composed/v1 Extension
section.t: The composed/v1 extension kind carries an evidence set built from the answers of several responders as one portable object. Each responder answered one Evidence Request () with exactly one of three outcomes:

li.t: an artifact, here an Evidence Bundle;
a signed refusal;
a recorded absence.

section.t: Each answer is a member of the composition. The block declares:

li.t: each member's digest and outcome;
the observer that produced each member;
the joins between members;
a composed digest that a judgment or other record can cite as the exact evidence set it was made from.

section.t: The containing Bundle is an ordinary evidence-bundle/v2. Its root is the composing party's own record, and its core checks apply unchanged. The extension adds a set of member bundles alongside that record; it does not change what records, root or completeness mean.

section.name: Block
section.t: The block is a JSON object conforming to this CDDL :

A join's pointer and each compare element are JSON Pointers . Member id values are unique, and so are observer id values. Every member's observer names a declared observer. Every join names two distinct declared members, in ascending order. No two joins share the same members, basis and pointer. not_requested names participants that the composing party knew of but did not ask. A participant listed there is not a member, and its identifier MUST NOT also appear as a member id. A block that violates any of these rules is malformed. A verifier reports a malformed block as a failed composed/v1 check and MUST NOT report any composition result from it.

section.name: Members and Outcomes
section.t: A member records the outcome of one request to one responder, and nothing else. The three outcomes are those of . They are never converted into one another:

li.t: A refusal member exists only when the responder signed a refusal.
A timeout is an absence, never a refusal.
A received refusal is never recorded as an absence.
A request still inside its waiting window is pending. Pending is not an outcome, so a pending request MUST NOT be composed as a member.

section.t: digest depends on the outcome:

li.t: For artifact, it is the member Evidence Bundle's bundle digest ().
For refusal and absence, it is the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of the UTF-8 JCS serialization of the refusal or absence object, as carried.

section.t: When the body (bundle, refusal or absence) is carried, a verifier MUST recompute digest from it. For a refusal or absence, it MUST also require the body's request_digest to equal the member's. A refusal's signature is verified under the deployment's signature profile. A verifier that does not implement that profile reports the refusal as signature-unverified. It does not report it as failed, and it does not report it as absent.

An artifact member MAY carry response: the responder's signed response to the request, as received, with the artifact bytes removed. A response signature that names the artifact by digest therefore still verifies without them. When the bundle and response are both carried, a verifier MUST require the response's request_digest to equal the member's, and its artifact_digest to equal the member's digest. Either mismatch is a failed composed/v1 check. This binds the artifact to the request it answered, as a refusal's or absence's own request_digest does. The response's signature is verified under the deployment's signature profile, exactly as a refusal's is. A verifier that does not implement that profile reports the response as signature-unverified, which is neither failed nor absent. response is not part of the composed digest ().

An artifact that fails verification is still an artifact member. The verifier reports the failure on that member. It is not a fourth outcome, and the verifier MUST NOT report it as a successful grant.
An empty-history Bundle () is an artifact member that shows no history. It is neither a failure nor an absence. A responder whose history was cleared, or never started, can answer with one.

Each member keeps its own claims. A verifier MUST verify every carried member bundle as an Evidence Bundle under this document. It MUST report that bundle's graph closure, interval coverage and per-record membership (), and its disclosures and countersignatures, per member.

The verifier MUST NOT merge one member's claims with another member's, or with the containing Bundle's. The containing Bundle's claims are about its own records only. A refusal or absence member is not a failed claim: a verifier reports it as what it is.

section.name: Composition Closure
section.t: A composed/v1 block makes a fourth completeness claim, composition closure. It holds when every member is either:

li.t: present, meaning its body is carried and reproduces its digest; or
declared missing, meaning its id is listed in missing and it carries no body.

section.t: The claim has three results:

li.t: pass: every member is present and missing is absent or empty.
withheld (finding declared_incomplete): every member is present or declared missing, and at least one is declared missing.
fail: in any of these cases:
a member neither carries a body nor is listed in missing;
a listed member carries a body;
a carried body does not reproduce its digest;
missing names an undeclared member.

section.t: A verifier MUST report composition closure separately from the three per-member claims and from the containing Bundle's claims. It MUST NOT report it as one of them.
Declaring a member missing withholds its body, not its existence. Its id, observer, request_digest, outcome and digest remain in the composed digest.
Composition closure covers declared members only. A participant that is in neither members nor not_requested is not visible to a verifier from this block ().

section.name: Controller Binding Records
section.t: A controller binding record is a JSON object in which the holders of two signing keys both sign one statement about how the two keys are related. It is the linkage evidence of the controller_binding join basis (). Its signatures show only that whoever held each private key signed the record. They do not show who holds either key, and this document never states who a key holder is.

A binding record is not a member of the composed/v1 block. It is delivered beside the containing Bundle, with any revocation statements that withdraw it; how they are delivered is outside this document. The block binds a record only through a join's identifier_digest.

In this section a key identifier is 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters; for an Ed25519 key, the one key type this document defines, it is the raw 32-byte public key. A time is an date-time in UTC with a "Z" suffix and seconds precision. A root record's timestamp, against which a binding is checked, can also carry fractional seconds. Times compare as instants.
The claim types, the member each adds, the method this document defines for each, and what the two key holders state:

li.t: same_controller_asserted: no added member; dual_signature/0. One controller holds both keys.
delegated_by: adds delegator; dual_signature/0. The holder of delegator delegated to the holder of the other key, who accepted.

section.t: A binding record is malformed when it lacks a member, carries a member the CDDL does not list, or has a value outside its form; when it carries delegator and its claim is not delegated_by, or credential and its claim is not same_organization_credentialed, or lacks the member its claim adds; when its two keys are equal or not in ascending order; when not_before is later than issued_at or not_after is not later than it; when nonce is empty; when delegator is not one of keys; when both keys are ed25519 keys and a sig is not a sig-hex; or when its method is one this document defines for another claim type. A method token this document does not define is well formed. A binding record or revocation statement that is not a JSON object is malformed. delegated_by states a relation, not a scope: a verifier reads no authority from it.

Key types. key_types, when present, names the type of each key in keys, in its order. When it is absent, both keys are ed25519 keys. This document defines one key type, ed25519: the key identifier is the raw Ed25519 public key, and the key signs with Ed25519. A record whose key_types names any other token is well formed. Its sig values are not held to sig-hex, and a verifier that does not implement that key type treats the record as under a method it does not implement.

Signing input and binding digest. The signing input is the UTF-8 octets of the JCS serialization of the record without sigs. Every other member is covered. The binding digest is the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of the signing input. It does not cover sigs, so a binding keeps its digest if a key signs it again. Two ceremonies over the same keys differ in nonce and so have two digests.

Methods. Under dual_signature/0, sigs has exactly two entries: sigs[0].key_id is keys[0], sigs[1].key_id is keys[1], and each sig is that key's signature over the signing input; for an ed25519 key, its Ed25519 signature in lowercase hexadecimal. A record with one signature, a third entry, or a signature that does not verify is not signed by both keys. One key cannot bind another key to itself, because each key signs the other key's identifier. dual_signature_credential/0 requires the same two signatures. Its credential names a signed object from the key credential.issuer, delivered beside the record, whose SHA-256 is credential.digest and which is verified by its native method credential.method. This document registers no credential format. A credential never decides whether a binding applies, and a verifier MUST NOT present the organization it names as an identity.

Revocation. Either key holder can withdraw a binding with a revocation statement (binding-revocation). A statement applies to a binding when it is well formed, binding is the binding digest, key_id is one of the binding's keys, and sig is that key's Ed25519 signature over the UTF-8 JCS serialization of the statement without sig. A statement names a binding by digest, so it reaches every copy of the record. From revoked_at on, the binding is not in effect. revoked_at is the revoking key holder's statement; a backdated revocation returns the joins it covered to unjoined, never further. A verifier knows only the statements it received.
When a binding applies. A binding record applies to two key identifiers at a set of times T when all of these hold:

li.t: it is well formed;
the verifier implements its method and the type of both keys, and both bound keys signed it under that method;
its keys are exactly the two key identifiers, in either order;
for every T, not_before <= T < not_after;
no revocation statement the verifier received that applies to it has a revoked_at at or before any T.

section.t: What a binding never states. A binding is a statement by both key holders that their two keys are not independent issuers. A verifier MUST NOT present a binding record as establishing who controls either key; a person, name, account, organization identity or legal relationship; that the keys were under one control at any time, beyond the window and claim both key holders stated; or that two keys with no binding between them have distinct controllers.

section.name: Joins
section.t: A join declares that two members' records are about the same thing, and how that is established. The producer DECLARES a state; a verifier DERIVES it again from the carried members. A declaration that does not match the derivation is a failed composed/v1 check (finding join_state_mismatch). It is never a pass.
The states derive as follows:

li.t: one_sided: exactly one of the two members has outcome artifact with records, and the other has none: it is not an artifact, or it is an empty-history Bundle (). Under controller_binding, a join with an empty-history member is one_sided only when the two are linked (below).

unjoined: neither member has outcome artifact with records; or one has records, the other is an empty-history Bundle, and the controller_binding linkage does not link them; or both have records, but the linkage basis does not establish that their records are about the same thing.

agree: both members are artifacts with records and are linked, and every compare pointer resolves in both root records to values with identical JCS serializations. A join with no compare and a link is agree.
mismatch: both members are artifacts with records and are linked, and at least one compare pointer resolves to different values, or does not resolve on one side.

section.t: Linkage is evaluated on each artifact member's root record (its bundle's root). This document defines the derivation for three bases:

li.t: pre_agreed_identifier: pointer selects a string in each root record. The members are linked when SHA-256 of that string's UTF-8 octets equals identifier_digest on both sides. The identifier itself never enters the block.
shared_artifact_digest: pointer selects a digest string in each root record. The members are linked when the two values are identical.

controller_binding: pointer selects a key identifier string in each root record, for example /key_id, and identifier_digest is a binding digest (). The members are linked when a delivered binding record whose binding digest equals identifier_digest applies to the two selected values, with T the timestamp of each root record (). A verifier that received no record with that digest, or only well-formed records with that digest whose method or key types it does not implement, reports the join as not_derivable; so does a join without pointer or identifier_digest. Any other record with that digest that does not apply (malformed, not signed by both keys, other keys, outside its window, or revoked) leaves the members unjoined. A join on this basis states that the two root records are under keys whose holders bound them, as both of them stated it; it says nothing about who those holders are.

When one member is an empty-history Bundle (), the derivation still runs. That member's key identifier is the key that signed its checkpoint.cose, as that signature authenticates it, and its T is that checkpoint's timestamp; pointer selects the key identifier in the other member's root record only. Linked gives one_sided, never agree, because nothing was compared; not linked gives unjoined. An empty-history member without a checkpoint.cose that verifies has no key, and the join is not_derivable.

section.t: The bases issued_receipt (the two records cite one Receipt) and same_interval (the two records fall in one declared interval) are reserved for a later specification that defines their derivation. A block MAY declare joins on them; such joins are digest-covered. A verifier that does not implement a derivation for the basis reports such a join as not_derivable. It MUST NOT report the join as a derived agreement, and MUST NOT count it as corroboration.
A join one of whose artifact members is declared missing is also not_derivable.
On a derived mismatch, a verifier reports each member's value at each differing pointer, and names no winner.

section.name: Observers and Redundancy
section.t: observers[] states, for each member, which observer produced it, in what role, and in which custody_domain. role is a short token naming where the observer sits, for example responder, runtime or network_boundary; this document does not define a role vocabulary, and a verifier reports the role without interpreting it. A custody domain is an opaque label that the composing party assigns. Two observers are in the same custody domain exactly when their labels are identical octet sequences.
Same custody is redundant, not corroborating. For every join that derives agree, a verifier MUST report the pair as redundant in any of these cases:

li.t: both members name the same observer;
the two observers have the same custody_domain;
the two members' root records carry the same key_id;
the join's basis is controller_binding: the holders of the two keys have stated that the keys are not independent issuers ().

section.t: It MUST present the result as "redundant, not corroborating", with the reason. A controller_binding join therefore never yields corroboration. Otherwise it MAY report the pair as corroborating, and it MUST qualify that as resting on declared custody.

Custody labels are the composing party's declaration. Like producer-key/v1 (), they can only downgrade a result. Identical labels make a pair redundant. Distinct labels never establish that two observers are independent, and a verifier MUST NOT present them as doing so.
Corroboration is derived; it is never declared, and it is not part of the block. A verifier lists results per pair. It MUST NOT combine them into a count or score.

section.name: Composed Digest
section.t: The composed digest is the digest a judgment cites as the evidence set it was made from. It is computed only from the declarations in the block, so it recomputes from the containing Bundle alone. It stays the same whether or not the member bodies are carried.

li.t: Build the digest input D, a JSON object with exactly these five members:
kind: the string "composed/v1".
members: for each member, an object with exactly its id, observer, request_digest, outcome and digest. Sort the objects in ascending order of id.
observers: for each observer, an object with exactly its id, role and custody_domain. Sort in ascending order of id.

joins: for each join, an object with its members, basis and state, plus whichever of pointer, identifier_digest and compare the join carries (absent members stay absent, never null). Sort in ascending order of members[0], then members[1], then basis, then pointer (the empty string when absent). compare keeps its carried order. Use [] when the block has no joins.
not_requested: the block's not_requested sorted ascending, or [] when it has none.
Identifiers are ASCII (label-id), so ascending order is octet order. The order in which arrays are carried does not affect the digest.

composed_digest is the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of the UTF-8 octets of the JCS serialization of D. This is the canonicalization algorithm jcs of : RFC 8785 with no normalization pass, SHA-256, bare hex. D contains no numbers.
Member bodies, each member's response, missing and composed_digest itself are excluded.

section.t: A verifier MUST recompute composed_digest and report a mismatch as a failed composed/v1 check. It MUST NOT report the recomputed value as the digest of any member, nor as the containing Bundle's digest.

The containing Bundle's own digest () still covers the whole block, bodies included. A countersignature over the containing Bundle therefore binds the composition and everything carried with it. The composed digest binds only the evidence set.

Because the composed digest covers each member's outcome, observer and digest, all observers' roles and custody labels, and every join declaration, changing any of them changes the composed digest. A judgment that cites a composed digest therefore also binds the declared custody, and with it the redundancy result a verifier derives from that custody.

section.name: Verifying composed/v1
section.t: A verifier that implements composed/v1 MUST report each of the following separately:

li.t: the recomputed composed digest, and whether it matches;

per member: outcome, body carried or declared missing, digest reproduced, and, for a carried member bundle, its own three completeness claims, no history for an empty-history Bundle (), and, when it carries response, whether the response's digests match and its signature state;
composition closure;
per join: the declared state, the derived state (or not_derivable), and whether they match;
per derived agree: redundant (with reason) or corroborating on declared custody.

section.t: A verifier that does not implement composed/v1 follows : it reports the block as uninterpreted and integrity-covered. It MUST NOT present any member, join or composed digest as checked.

section.name: Provisional Extension Kinds
section.t: The interim registry () also records two extension kinds held for ratification and not registered: sd-jwt-issuers/v1, the issuer keys under which SD-JWT presentations in a revealed agent_input are verified offline, and disclosure-policy-decisions/v1, the per-Capsule disclosure-policy decision that a constraint record binds by digest. This document does not define them. A verifier that does not implement them treats them as it treats any extension kind it does not implement (): digest-covered and uninterpreted.

section.name: Bundle Digest and Countersignatures
section.t: The bundle digest is SHA-256(UTF8(JCS(canonical bundle form))), rendered as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. The canonical bundle form is the Bundle with countersignatures omitted. countersignatures is excluded so that independent parties can add signatures without changing the digest they sign; every other present Bundle member, including extensions, participates.

countersignatures, when present, is an array of objects. Each object MUST carry type and the type's signature encoding, and signs the bundle digest. An object whose signer is a party other than the producer is a countersignature (). This document does not define who populates the slot or whether a relying party should rely on a given signer.

The registered types are cose-sign1 and countersign/v1. A cose-sign1 object is {type: "cose-sign1", signature: "<base64url tagged COSE_Sign1>"}. It is a reserved neutral slot whose population and verification are future scope; a current verifier MUST surface each such entry as unverified and MUST NOT present pass-through data as a verified countersignature. The countersign/v1 object is defined in . A verifier MUST report an entry of a type it does not implement as unverified and MUST NOT let it change any other result. An entry with no type member is the legacy form of countersign/v1. A verifier MUST process it as countersign/v1, and its signing input then uses the value countersign/v1 for type. A producer MUST NOT emit the legacy form.

section.name: The countersign/v1 Entry
section.t: type, signer, over, statement, and signature are REQUIRED; receipt is OPTIONAL.

signer.id identifies the countersigner, for example a did:web identifier. signer.key_id is the countersigner's 32-byte Ed25519 public key as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters: the key itself, not a digest of it, so that a verifier holding only the entry can check the signature offline.
over is the bundle digest () of the Bundle the countersigner recomputed.
statement says what the countersigner recomputed and with what result.

li.t: checks is a non-empty array. Each element names one check in name, a short phrase for what was recomputed, and gives its result, which is exactly one of the five values below. A check name is unique within a statement.
recomputed_at is the UTC time, with a "Z" suffix, at which the countersigner finished recomputing.

scope.ledger_id identifies the ledger whose records the Bundle carries, as the issuer identified it to the countersigner. scope.closure_depth is the closure depth the countersigner applied (). scope.period, when present, is the {from, to} interval of timestamps the checks covered; it is absent when the Bundle declares no such interval.

tr.td: The check ran and its condition held.
The check ran and its condition did not hold.
The Bundle carries nothing this check operates on.
The check could not run, for example because there was nothing to compare against.
The check ran but resolved only in part.

section.t: Each result stands alone. A statement MUST NOT carry an aggregate result, a score, a rating, or a claim of compliance, and a verifier MUST NOT derive one from the checks. Capture coverage, meaning whether every action that occurred was recorded, cannot be recomputed from the records a Bundle carries; a statement MUST NOT report it as a check result. Profile identifiers naming a recomputation policy, when a later revision adds them, use the countersign. prefix; this document defines none.

signature is the Ed25519 signature, as 128 lowercase hexadecimal characters, over the signing input UTF8(JCS({"over": over, "signer": signer, "statement": statement, "type": type})). The signature binds the Bundle, the signer's identity and what the countersigner says about it; signer is the entry's signer object exactly as it appears on the wire.

receipt, when present, is a Receipt showing the statement was registered with a Transparency Service, in that service's receipt encoding. A verifier that cannot verify it MUST report it as unverified; its absence does not invalidate the entry.
A verifier MUST ignore entry members not defined here, and they MUST NOT change any result it reports.

section.name: Verifying a countersign/v1 Entry
section.t: A verifier MUST, for each countersign/v1 entry:

li.t: determine independence as in .

section.t: A verifier MAY resolve signer.key_id against a directory of countersigners that it or the relying party chooses, to put a name to the key. No directory is privileged, and this document defines none. A verifier reports each countersign/v1 entry as exactly one of invalid, not independent, unresolved signer (independent, and the key is in no directory consulted), or resolved (independent, and the key is found). It MUST attribute each check and result to the signer, as the signer's statement, and MUST NOT present them as its own findings.

section.name: Self-Countersignature
section.t: A countersignature is a self-countersignature when signer.key_id equals the producer's key: the kid of a Producer Envelope over any record in records (), the public_key of a well-formed producer-key/v1 extension (), or any other key the verifier holds for that producer. A self-countersignature is a well-formed entry that does not meet the definition of a countersignature, because its signer is the producer. A verifier MUST NOT reject it for being one, and MUST render it as not independent, never as a countersignature by a party other than the producer. The verifier computes independence itself for each entry; no entry member and no directory entry can change that result, and a producer key declaration can only change it to not independent.

section.name: Fragment Codec
section.t: The common permalink codec is exact. To encode a Bundle in a URL fragment, a producer MUST serialize the whole Bundle with JCS, including recursive sort_keys object-member ordering, UTF-8 encode the resulting JSON text, and encode those bytes with RFC 4648 base64url Section 5 without padding. The resulting unescaped ASCII string is the fragment value after #. A decoder MUST base64url-decode the unpadded fragment, UTF-8 decode it, parse it as JSON, and then apply the Bundle checks in this document.

The /v/<id> route carries a Bundle of one using this same codec; /bundle uses no different decoder. The path is a locator only. URL fragments are not sent in HTTP requests, so a hosted service receives a Bundle only when it is otherwise uploaded or embedded in the returned report.

section.name: Verification
section.t: verification, when present, is producer self-report. It MAY record tool versions, performed checks, or findings, but it is not proof and MUST NOT replace independent verification of Capsules, disclosures, closure, certificates, checkpoints, or countersignatures. A verifier MUST label it as producer self-report.

A conforming verifier MUST at minimum compute the Bundle digest, verify each enclosed Capsule under the base profile, apply and , and report graph closure, interval coverage, and per-record membership as separate results. It MUST distinguish WITHHELD, REVEALED-match, REVEALED-mismatch, declared incomplete, and absent or invalid membership proofs. It MUST apply to every Bundle, so that a certificate mode it does not implement is reported as not established, never as failed.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: The Bundle does not make omitted evidence disappear. Its explicit missing declaration is necessary to prevent a short report from being represented as a complete closure. Range endpoints are not a substitute for per-record membership: endpoint-only proofs leave interior substitution and deletion undetected. Disclosures are not signatures and are untrusted until their DE-3 digest comparison succeeds. Fragments can be copied or changed by a party hosting a link, so every received Bundle requires independent verification. Unknown extension kinds are integrity-covered but semantically untrusted.

A producer-selected certificate proves that each carried record is in the log; it says nothing about the records the producer left out, so a verifier never presents one as complete (). Reporting an unimplemented certificate mode as not established rather than invalid keeps a failure meaningful: a verifier that reported every unfamiliar mode as invalid would report an honest Bundle and an altered one identically. The cost is a downgrade: whoever alters a Bundle can name an unknown mode, or put a non-record leaf of an undefined type where a record or a padding leaf was, and so turn a failing per-record membership into one that is not established (, ). Neither change can make a claim established. A relying party therefore treats "not established" as unverified, never as a pass. A padding leaf is accepted only with its full content, never as a bare digest, because a bare leaf value could be the identifier of a Capsule the producer chose not to show; recomputing the value from padding content, whose only free member is a random nonce, rules that out ().

A countersignature's statement and signer are what a relying party reads, so both are inside the signing input (); a signature over the bundle digest alone would let anyone holding the Bundle rewrite a failed result as established, or attribute the entry to a different signer identifier, without detection. A verified signature establishes who made the statement, not that the relying party should rely on that party: signer trust, and the choice of any directory used to put a name to a key, are outside this document. A self-countersignature is not a second party's check, and rendering it as one would present the producer's own claim as independent corroboration; forbids that. A producer-key/v1 declaration can only cause an entry to be reported as not independent: a producer that declares a key it does not hold weakens only its own Bundle's countersignatures, and a producer that countersigns with a key it does not declare is still reported at most as an unresolved signer unless a directory the verifier chose lists that key. Results are listed per check and never combined, because an aggregate would hide a failed or not checked result behind a total.

li.t: Omitted participants. The composing party chooses whom to list. Composition closure proves that every declared member is present or declared missing. It cannot reveal a participant that the composing party never listed. not_requested makes a known omission explicit. Completeness against the real set of participants needs an independent statement of that set, such as a coordinator's sealed topology. A verifier MUST NOT describe composition closure as completeness of participation.
Declarations versus derivations. Declared join states are re-derived; a mismatch fails. Declared custody can only downgrade (). Nothing a producer declares can make two observers independent.

Controller bindings. A binding can only make an agreement redundant (); no binding, revocation or failed signature can make two members corroborating. Two keys bound by their holders can sign agreeing records, and without the redundancy rule they would read as two issuers. A verifier knows only the revocation statements it received: the party presenting a composition can leave out a revocation, and a controller_binding agreement is then reported redundant all the same, never more. A revocation the producer did not account for derives unjoined and fails a declared agree (join_state_mismatch).

No history. An empty-history Bundle () is its producer's statement that its stream holds no record. Its signed checkpoint shows that the stream exists, under which key, and the size of its log at that time. It carries no certificate, so nothing shows that no leaf of that log is a record. A verifier MUST NOT present no history as evidence that no action took place. Because it is an artifact, never an absence, a cleared or unstarted history cannot be read as a responder that did not answer.
Outcomes. Keeping refusal and absence distinct is evidentiary: synthesizing either one from the other forges the stronger record from the weaker.

section.name: Category Coverage
section.t: A category declaration is the producer's statement about itself (). A producer that chooses its own categories can declare whatever is favorable to it; this is why a private set is never reported as registered, and why a verifier reports properties rather than a verdict of completeness. A signed ABSENT is attributable and can be contradicted by records a counterparty holds, but it is not evidence that nothing exists. Including the Bundle's root in the signing input stops a declaration made for one root record from being presented with another; a countersignature over the bundle digest is what binds it to the whole Bundle.

section.name: Privacy Considerations
section.t: A Bundle reveals a preimage only through its disclosure overlay (); a member absent from the overlay stays WITHHELD.

A range that carries padding leaves () shows where padding runs begin and end, and padding is appended before a checkpoint is cut. Such a range therefore reveals some of the log's earlier checkpoint sizes, which padding exists to blur (Section 12.1 of ). A producer that does not want to show them uses a producer-selected certificate (), which carries no positions other than those of the records it carries.
A cleared history's empty-history Bundle () carries a checkpoint signed by the same key as the cleared stream. Clearing a history therefore does not unlink that key from it.
For the composed/v1 extension ():

li.t: Join identifiers enter only as digests (identifier_digest).

A delivered controller binding record () reveals that the holders of its two keys bound them, its claim type and its window. It carries no name, and it is delivered only to whom the presenting party chooses.
custody_domain is an opaque label and SHOULD NOT be a network address, an account identifier or a personal name.
Withholding a member's body (missing) keeps the composed digest stable. A judgment can therefore be checked against a composition presented to an audience that may not see every member.

section.name: IANA Considerations
section.t: IANA is requested to create the "AAC Evidence Bundle Parameters" registry group with these Specification Required registries, using and terminology and the designated-expert criteria of :

li.t: "Evidence Bundle kind", initial value evidence-bundle/v2.

"Evidence Bundle extension kind", initial values producer-key/v1 () and composed/v1 (). A registered specification defines each block; private x- prefixed kinds are not registered. The kinds sd-jwt-issuers/v1 and disclosure-policy-decisions/v1 () are not initial values.
"Evidence Bundle countersignature type", initial values cose-sign1 () and countersign/v1 ().

"Evidence Bundle category set", with no initial values. Each entry registers a category set identifier for category_coverage (), its category names, and how a record is assigned to a category. The registering specification names any external source of the categories by version. Identifiers beginning x- are private and are not registered.

section.t: Until IANA registry creation, the interim registry of record is REGISTRY.md in the source repository of . It records the same values and policy.

front.title: Key words for use in RFCs to Indicate Requirement Levels

abstract.t: In many standards track documents several words are used to signify the requirements in the specification. These words are often capitalized. This document defines these words as they should be interpreted in IETF documents. This document specifies an Internet Best Current Practices for the Internet Community, and requests discussion and suggestions for improvements.

front.title: Ambiguity of Uppercase vs Lowercase in RFC 2119 Key Words

abstract.t: RFC 2119 specifies common key words that may be used in protocol specifications. This document aims to reduce the ambiguity by clarifying that only UPPERCASE usage of the key words have the defined special meanings.

front.title: Guidelines for Writing an IANA Considerations Section in RFCs

abstract.t: Many protocols make use of points of extensibility that use constants to identify various protocol parameters. To ensure that the values in these fields do not have conflicting uses and to promote interoperability, their allocations are often coordinated by a central record keeper. For IETF protocols, that role is filled by the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA).

To make assignments in a given registry prudently, guidance describing the conditions under which new values should be assigned, as well as when and how modifications to existing values can be made, is needed. This document defines a framework for the documentation of these guidelines by specification authors, in order to assure that the provided guidance for the IANA Considerations is clear and addresses the various issues that are likely in the operation of a registry.
This is the third edition of this document; it obsoletes RFC 5226.

front.title: The JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) Data Interchange Format

abstract.t: JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) is a lightweight, text-based, language-independent data interchange format. It was derived from the ECMAScript Programming Language Standard. JSON defines a small set of formatting rules for the portable representation of structured data.
This document removes inconsistencies with other specifications of JSON, repairs specification errors, and offers experience-based interoperability guidance.

front.title: JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS)

abstract.t: Cryptographic operations like hashing and signing need the data to be expressed in an invariant format so that the operations are reliably repeatable. One way to address this is to create a canonical representation of the data. Canonicalization also permits data to be exchanged in its original form on the "wire" while cryptographic operations performed on the canonicalized counterpart of the data in the producer and consumer endpoints generate consistent results.

This document describes the JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS). This specification defines how to create a canonical representation of JSON data by building on the strict serialization methods for JSON primitives defined by ECMAScript, constraining JSON data to the Internet JSON (I-JSON) subset, and by using deterministic property sorting.

front.title: The Base16, Base32, and Base64 Data Encodings

abstract.t: This document describes the commonly used base 64, base 32, and base 16 encoding schemes. It also discusses the use of line-feeds in encoded data, use of padding in encoded data, use of non-alphabet characters in encoded data, use of different encoding alphabets, and canonical encodings. [STANDARDS-TRACK]

front.title: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps

abstract.t: This document defines a date and time format for use in Internet protocols that is a profile of the ISO 8601 standard for representation of dates and times using the Gregorian calendar.

front.title: Edwards-Curve Digital Signature Algorithm (EdDSA)

abstract.t: This document describes elliptic curve signature scheme Edwards-curve Digital Signature Algorithm (EdDSA). The algorithm is instantiated with recommended parameters for the edwards25519 and edwards448 curves. An example implementation and test vectors are provided.

front.title: Concise Data Definition Language (CDDL): A Notational Convention to Express Concise Binary Object Representation (CBOR) and JSON Data Structures

abstract.t: This document proposes a notational convention to express Concise Binary Object Representation (CBOR) data structures (RFC 7049). Its main goal is to provide an easy and unambiguous way to express structures for protocol messages and data formats that use CBOR or JSON.

front.title: JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) Pointer

abstract.t: JSON Pointer defines a string syntax for identifying a specific value within a JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) document.

front.title: An Architecture for Trustworthy and Transparent Digital Supply Chains

abstract.t: Traceability in supply chains is a growing security concern. While Verifiable Data Structures (VDSs) have addressed specific issues, such as equivocation over digital certificates, they lack a universal architecture for all supply chains. This document defines such an architecture for single-issuer signed statement transparency. It ensures extensibility and interoperability between different transparency services as well as compliance with various auditing procedures and regulatory requirements.

front.title: CBOR Object Signing and Encryption (COSE) Receipts

abstract.t: CBOR Object Signing and Encryption (COSE) Receipts prove properties of a Verifiable Data Structure (VDS) to a verifier. VDSs and associated Proof Types enable security properties, such as minimal disclosure, transparency, and non-equivocation. Transparency helps maintain trust over time and has been applied to certificates, end-to-end encrypted messaging systems, and supply chain security. This specification enables concise transparency-oriented systems by building on Concise Binary Object Representation (CBOR) and COSE. The extensibility of the approach is demonstrated by providing CBOR encodings for Merkle inclusion and consistency proofs.

front.title: An Agent Action Capsule Profile for SCITT
Disclosure Envelope Profile for Agent Action Capsules
An Interaction Model for Requesting Verifiable Evidence
Uniform Resource Identifier (URI): Generic Syntax

abstract.t: A Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) is a compact sequence of characters that identifies an abstract or physical resource. This specification defines the generic URI syntax and a process for resolving URI references that might be in relative form, along with guidelines and security considerations for the use of URIs on the Internet. The URI syntax defines a grammar that is a superset of all valid URIs, allowing an implementation to parse the common components of a URI reference without knowing the scheme-specific requirements of every possible identifier. This specification does not define a generative grammar for URIs; that task is performed by the individual specifications of each URI scheme. [STANDARDS-TRACK]

front.title: Evidence Layer
Canonicalization Declaration for SCITT Signed Statements
CBOR Object Signing and Encryption (COSE): Countersignatures

abstract.t: Concise Binary Object Representation (CBOR) is a data format designed for small code size and small message size. CBOR Object Signing and Encryption (COSE) defines a set of security services for CBOR. This document defines a countersignature algorithm along with the needed header parameters and CBOR tags for COSE. This document updates RFC 9052.

front.title: Selective Disclosure for JSON Web Tokens

abstract.t: This specification defines a mechanism for the selective disclosure of individual elements of a JSON data structure used as the payload of a JSON Web Signature (JWS). The primary use case is the selective disclosure of JSON Web Token (JWT) claims.

section.name: Change Log
section.t: Since -01:

li.t: Certificate modes (): completeness.selection names the mode of completeness_certificate; a verifier reports a mode it does not implement as not established (certificate_mode_unsupported), never as failed or invalid.

Defined the producer-selected certificate (), in the shape producers already emit: selection producer-selected, no range, each record proven on its own; interval coverage is never established for it. Added none to payloads_mode.

Non-record leaves (): a range covers padding leaves in completeness_certificate.non_record_leaves, each carried in full; stated the padding leaf's serialization and identifier, the per-position accounting rule for per-record membership, and that a leaf of an undefined type leaves the claim not established, never established. Stated that per-record membership is the claim, and that unknown completeness_certificate members are ignored. Privacy Considerations: what a padded range reveals. Security Considerations: reporting an unimplemented mode or an undefined leaf type as not established can turn a failure into not established, never into established; why a padding leaf is carried in full.

Category coverage (): the OPTIONAL category_coverage member, a producer's signed declaration of one status per category of a named category set (AVAILABLE, PARTIAL, WITHHELD, DELETED, ABSENT, UNDISCLOSED; UNDISCLOSED requires policy_uri), answering the Evidence Request categories field; five verifier properties, reported separately and never combined; it declares and does not prove. Created the "Evidence Bundle category set" registry, with no initial values. The Abstract mentions the declaration.

composed/v1: defined the controller binding record (): its members and claim types, its signing input and binding digest, the methods dual_signature/0 and dual_signature_credential/0, revocation statements, and when a binding applies; and the controller_binding join basis with its derivation (). A controller_binding agreement is always redundant, never corroborating (). A verifier that implements only -01 reads a block that carries a controller_binding join as malformed, since -01's join-basis does not list it. Security and Privacy Considerations: controller bindings. A binding record MAY carry key_types; this document defines the ed25519 key type, and a record under any other is treated as under a method a verifier does not implement.

Empty-history Bundles (): a Bundle with no records and no root shows that a stream has no history to disclose, whether it was never started or its history was cleared (a new stream, with a new log_id). It is well formed and reported as no history, never as failed and never as an absence. In composed/v1 it is an artifact member, and a join with it derives one_sided; a controller_binding join derives from the key that signed its checkpoint, and is not_derivable without one. Security Considerations: no history. Privacy Considerations: a cleared history's checkpoint is signed by the cleared stream's key.
Cites Evidence Request -01 and, informatively, Evidence Layer -00 and the Canonicalization Declaration -06.

section.t: Since -00:

li.t: Countersignatures: defined the countersign/v1 countersignature entry, its statement, and its five check results; defined countersignature, countersigner, and self-countersignature, and required a self-countersignature to be rendered as not independent; registered countersign/v1 as a second countersignature type; an entry with no type is processed as countersign/v1 (the legacy form).
Defined and registered the producer-key/v1 extension kind, which declares the producer's key and can only cause a countersignature to be reported as not independent.

Defined and registered the composed/v1 extension kind: one member per responder carrying its Evidence Request outcome (artifact, refusal or absence); observers with a role and a custody domain; joins whose declared state (agree, mismatch, unjoined or one_sided) a verifier re-derives; a fourth completeness claim, composition closure; same-custody agreement reported as redundant, not corroborating; and a composed digest (JCS, SHA-256) over the member, observer, join and not_requested declarations. Added Privacy Considerations.
Noted two provisional extension kinds, sd-jwt-issuers/v1 and disclosure-policy-decisions/v1, held for ratification in the interim registry and not defined by this document.
